title: DR1 names commodities and species the way a user would — Cattle, and "Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)" — while the frontend says Cow and gives the Latin name alone.

finding.frontend: Every species option is labelled with its scientific name and nothing else — Bison bison, Bos spp., Bos taurus, Bubalus bubalis, Equus caballus, Felis catus, Canis lupus familiaris, Salmo salar. The 0102 commodity is called Cow, in the checkbox legend "Cow (0102)" and again in the Common name column of the Selected commodities table on the consignment-details page. The labels come straight from the catalogue module, which stores only a scientific-name text per species (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:18-25).
finding.prototype: DR1 stores a common name alongside the scientific name and shows both in the search results, as "Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)", "African buffalo (Syncerus spp.)", "Water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis)" and "Yak (Poephagus spp.)". Where a species has no common name recorded, the scientific name stands alone. DR1 calls the 0102 commodity Cattle, in the search result header "Cattle (0102)" and in the Common name column of its own selected-commodities summary (app/data/commodities.js:11-24).
finding.difference: Record a common name against every species in the frontend catalogue and render the option label as "Common name (Scientific name)", falling back to the scientific name alone where no common name exists. Rename the 0102 commodity from Cow to Cattle, which changes the checkbox legend on the commodity page and the Common name cell on the consignment-details page. Note that DR1 uses the scientific name alone for the per-species subheadings on its own commodity-details page, so this change belongs to the option labels and the summary table, not to those subheadings.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a common name rendered anywhere in the frontend's species labels, or DR1 rendering a bare scientific name for a species that has a common name recorded against it.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and all three screenshots. DR1's result rows render as "African buffalo (Syncerus spp.)" and "Banteng (Novibos spp)" under a "Cattle (0102)" header (dr1-what-are-you-importing-results.html:286-306) and its selected-commodities row reads 0102 / Cattle (dr1-consignment-details.html:273-275); the frontend's eight labels are bare scientific names (fe-commodity-search.html:135-247) and its selected-commodities cell reads Cow (fe-consignment-details.html:132-133). Ran the falsifier both ways: no common name appears in any frontend species label, and every DR1 cattle species that has a commonName recorded renders it. Confirmed from the DOM rather than the page model, which on the commodity screen collapses all five fieldsets into one field. Claim CORRECT; the prototype citation lands on the wrong content — see correction.
finding.correction: The claim stands and the slots are left as written, but the prototype citation is wrong and the range should not simply be nudged. It cites app/data/commodities.js:11-24 for the common names; that range is the Cattle entry and holds no common name at all. The common names live in the species files it requires — app/data/commodities-0102-species.js:3-14 for the eleven cattle species, with app/data/commodities-0101-species.js and app/data/commodities-01061900-species.js for the other two shared files. Separately, this finding is narrower than its title suggests and deliberately so: Cow to Cattle is not the only commodity the two sides name differently, because the frontend's Fish is DR1's Ornamental fish. That pair differs in commodity code and in species as well as in name, so it is a catalogue-membership change rather than a rename and it has been folded into commodities--commodity-catalogue instead of duplicated here.
